neighbours.label: additive ' also' adding a further function or item to what was just stated ('They were also used for ...'); the top examples include the Japanese additive particle mo in the same role
fire: Windmills on the plain were built to grind corn. They were also used for pumping water out of the fields.
The fox feeds mainly on voles and mice. It also eats berries in late summer.
The harbour office issues fishing permits. It also keeps the register of all boats.
Besides repairing clocks, the old watchmaker also sold spectacles and barometers.
Clay tiles keep the rain out. They also help to keep the house cool in summer.
The treaty fixed the border along the river. It also gave both sides the right to fish there.
Otters hunt mostly at night. They are also seen at dawn near quiet streams.
The school teaches reading and arithmetic. Pupils also learn to swim in the lake.
quiet: Windmills on the plain were built to grind corn. They were seldom used for anything else.
The fox feeds mainly on voles and mice. It hunts them at dusk along the hedges.
The harbour office issues fishing permits. It opens at eight every morning.
Instead of repairing clocks, the old watchmaker mostly sold spectacles.
Clay tiles keep the rain out. They only crack in very hard frost.
The treaty fixed the border along the river. It was signed in the spring of 1820.
Otters hunt mostly at night. They rest during the day in burrows.
The school teaches reading and arithmetic. Pupils mainly come from nearby farms.

notes: Card: ' also' x8 plus Japanese mo / demo, and positions where an additive is due; the - pole's output promotes ' also', ' both' and suppresses ' primarily', ' mainly'. Probes: ' also' 0.20-0.48 in five sentences, 0.01-0.13 without it, 0.24 on 'as well as men'. The + pole also lists ' also' among its peaks, so the two poles are not a clean also/not-also split.
